extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (ESingular/Emacs users), computational algebraists who edit SINGULAR files and declare rings/orderings
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and standards for customizing the ESingular Emacs interface, editing SINGULAR input files in Emacs, and declaring rings/monomial orderings and using core SINGULAR algorithms/commands. Covers Emacs customization groups, recommended modes, ring declaration syntax, term ordering choices, quotient ring semantics, and algorithm/command usage notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entering Emacs customize environment
rubrics_metrics.description: You enter the customize environment by either calling M-x customize (on XEmacs you afterwards have to enter emacs in the minibuffer area) or by selecting the menu item Options->Customize->Emacs... for XEmacs, and the menu item Help->Customize->Toplevel Customization Group for Emacs, resp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A brief introduction to the customization mode comes up with the customization buffer. All customizable parameters are hierarchically grouped and you can browse through all these groups and change the values of the parameters using the mouse. At the end you can save your settings to a file making your changes permanent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing Singular Emacs customization group
rubrics_metrics.description: To change the settings of the Singular Emacs interface you can either select the item Preferences of the Singular menu, call M-x customize-group and give the argument singular-interactive, or browse from the top-level customization group through External->Singular->Singular interactive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Singular interface customization buffer is divided into four groups (Singular Faces; Singular Sections And Foldings; Singular Interactive Miscellaneous; Singular Demo Mode).

rubrics_metrics.name: Singular Faces
rubrics_metrics.description: Here you can specify various faces used if font-lock-mode is enabled (which, by default, is).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this group to change colors/fonts used for syntax highlighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Singular Sections And Foldings
rubrics_metrics.description: Here you can specify special faces for Singular input and output and change the text used as replacement for folded sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use customize-face-at-point to customize the face at point (function provided automatically by ESingular or add its definition to your .emacs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Singular Interactive Miscellaneous
rubrics_metrics.description: Here you can specify various things such as the behavior of the cursor keys, the name of the special Singular startup file, the appearance of the help window, or the default values for the singular command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tune interactive behavior of the ESingular buffer via this group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Singular Demo Mode customization
rubrics_metrics.description: Here you can specify how chunks of the demo file are divided, or specify a default directory for demo files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Configure demo chunking and file locations for demo mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where ESingular saves customized settings
rubrics_metrics.description: When you run ESingular, the settings of customized variables are saved in the file $HOME/.emacs-singular-cust. Otherwise, the settings are appended to your .emacs file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customized settings of ESingular are not automatically taken over by a "normal" Emacs, and vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Emacs C/C++-mode for SINGULAR files
rubrics_metrics.description: Since Singular’s programming language is similar to C, you should use the Emacs C/C++-mode to edit Singular input files and Singular libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C/C++-mode provides automatic indentation, line-breaking and keyword highlighting. ESingular turns on C/C++-mode automatically for files with suffix .sing or .lib; otherwise add auto-mode-alist entries to your .emacs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable font-lock-mode for C++-mode
rubrics_metrics.description: Turn on fontification for c++-mode (font-lock-mode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add a c++-mode-hook that calls (font-lock-mode 1) to enable syntax highlighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable auto-new-line and hungry-delete in C++-mode
rubrics_metrics.description: Turn on auto-new line and hungry-delete for C++-mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add a c++-mode-hook that calls (c-toggle-auto-hungry-state 1) to enable these editing conveniences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define customize-face-at-point helper
rubrics_metrics.description: A handy function for customization: customize-face-at-point – 'Customize face which point is at.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function inspects the face at point and calls customize-face on it; automatically defined when running ESingular, otherwise add its definition to your .emacs so you can easily change faces under point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customize source-code highlighting via Emacs Customize
rubrics_metrics.description: You can change the default settings for source-code highlighting (colors, fonts, etc.) by customizing the respective faces using the Customize feature of Emacs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use customize-face-at-point to quickly open the customization for the face under point.

rubrics_metrics.name: singular — start Singular with default arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: singular (menu Singular->Start Default...): starts Singular using default arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to launch a Singular process in the current buffer with configured defaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: singular-other — start Singular asking for arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: singular-other (menu Singular->Start): starts Singular asking for several arguments in the minibuffer area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you need to supply non-default startup arguments interactively.

rubrics_metrics.name: singular-exit — kill Singular process
rubrics_metrics.description: singular-exit (key C-c $ or menu Singular->Exit): kills the Singular process running in the current buffer (but does not kill the buffer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to terminate the running Singular process while preserving buffer contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: singular-restart — restart Singular preserving arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: singular-restart (key C-c C-r or menu Singular->Restart): kills the Singular process running in the current buffer and starts a new Singular process with exactly the same arguments as before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenient when the process needs restarting but arguments/settings should be preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: singular-beginning-of-line behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: singular-beginning-of-line (key C-a): moves point to beginning of line, then skips past the Singular prompt, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful navigation command tailored to ESingular prompt presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: singular-dynamic-complete (TAB) completion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: singular-dynamic-complete (key TAB): performs context specific completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If point is inside a string, file name completion is done. If point is at the end of a help command (help or ?), completion on Singular help topics is done. If point is at the end of an example command (example), completion is done on Singular examples. In all other cases, completion on Singular commands is done.

rubrics_metrics.name: singular-toggle-truncate-lines
rubrics_metrics.description: singular-toggle-truncate-lines (key C-c C-t or menu Commands->Truncate lines): toggles whether long lines should be truncated or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If lines are not truncated, use singular-scroll-left and singular-scroll-right to scroll horizontally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output folding commands
rubrics_metrics.description: singular-folding-toggle-fold-latest-output (C-c C-o), singular-folding-toggle-fold-at-point (C-c C-f), singular-folding-fold-all-output (menu Commands->Fold All Output), singular-folding-unfold-all-output (menu->Unfold All Output): commands to toggle/fold/unfold Singular output sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use folding to collapse huge outputs (toggle latest output or fold at point or fold/unfold all output sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Loading libraries and files
rubrics_metrics.description: singular-load-library (key C-c C-l) asks for a standard library name or a library file (TAB for completion) and loads the library; singular-load-file (key C-c <) asks for a file name (expanded with prefix arg) and loads the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Libraries submenu for standard libraries; TAB completion helps selecting names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Singular demo mode commands
rubrics_metrics.description: singular-demo-load (key C-c C-d): asks for a demo file and enters Singular demo mode showing first chunk; singular-demo-exit exits demo mode and cleans up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demo mode steps through demo chunks; customize chunking and default directory in Demo Mode settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help and example execution
rubrics_metrics.description: singular-help (key C-h C-s) asks for a help topic and shows help text; singular-example (key C-c C-e) asks for a Singular command and executes the example of this command in the current buffer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use help completion (TAB) and example execution to learn command usage from within Emacs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enter the Singular customization group
rubrics_metrics.description: customize-group (menu Singular->Preferences): enters the customization group of the Singular Emacs interface. (If called via M-x customize-group give argument singular-interactive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to jump directly to the SINGULAR-related customization options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithms require a prior ring definition
rubrics_metrics.description: All non-trivial algorithms in Singular require the prior definition of a ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before running standard-basis, Groebner, syzygy, factorization, etc., declare an appropriate ring (choose coefficient field/ring, variables, and monomial ordering).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported ring constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: A ring can be: 1) a polynomial ring over a field, 2) a polynomial ring over a ring, 3) a localization of 1., 4) a quotient ring by an ideal of 1. or 2., 5) a tensor product of 1. or 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except for quotient rings, specify coefficient field, variables, and appropriate global/local monomial ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available coefficient field/ring options
rubrics_metrics.description: The coefficient field of the rings may be: (1) QQ, (2) finite fields Z/p (p prime ≤ 2147483647), (3) GF(pn) with pn elements (p prime, pn ≤ 2^16), (4) transcendental extension of Q or Z/p, (5) simple algebraic extension of Q or Z/p, (6) field of real numbers as floating point of user-defined precision, (7) complex numbers represented by pairs of floating point numbers of user-defined precision, (8) the ring of integers (ZZ), (9) finite rings Z/m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain numeric/coefficient choices impose precision/approximation (real/complex floats are not exact); algebraic extensions may require setting minpoly; non-prime integer specs are converted to next lower prime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited functionality for non-field coefficient rings
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of coefficient rings, which are not fields, only the following functions are guaranteed to work: basic polynomial arithmetic (addition, multiplication, division, exponentiation), std (computing standard bases and related: syz, etc.), interred, reduce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect limited support on Z and Z/n; many higher-level algorithms may not be available or behave differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: The basering reserved name and switching
rubrics_metrics.description: The current active ring in Singular is called basering. The basering can be set by declaring a new ring or by using the commands setring and keepring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objects of ring-dependent types are local to a ring; to access them after changing basering map them using map, imap or fetch; use keepring as last statement in a procedure to make ring changes persistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objects local to ring and mapping semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects of ring dependent types are local to a ring. To access them after a change of the basering they have to be mapped using map or by the functions imap or fetch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing basering inside procedures is local unless keepring is used as final statement to persist change; use fetch to conveniently map objects between rings and quotient rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ring declaration syntax and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: ring name = (coefficients), (names of ring variables), (ordering); or ring name = cring [names of ring variables]. Purpose: declares a ring and sets it as the current basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default example: (ZZ/32003)[x,y,z]; cring stands for QQ, ZZ or (ZZ/m); second form sets ordering to (dp,C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Details on coefficient specification semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Coefficients may be a cring, a non-negative int expression less than 2^31 (0 for QQ or a prime p for Z/p), an int expression plus names for transcendental/algebraic extensions, a p^n spec for GF(p^n), 'real' or 'complex' with optional precision ints, or 'integer' with optional modulus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If int expression is not prime it is converted to next lower prime; algebraic extensions implemented for one parameter require minpoly assignment; GF(pn) faster than algebraic extension but limited to pn ≤ 2^15; real/complex use floating approximations and are not exact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering specification in ring declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: 'ordering' is a list of block orderings where each block ordering is either lp, dp, Dp, ls, ds, Ds optionally with size, or wp/Wp/ws/Ws/a followed by weight vector, or M(intmat) (matrix ordering), or c/C (component order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Block orderings produce product/block orderings; see Appendix B.2 for mathematical definitions. Parentheses may be omitted for single entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient ring (qring) syntax and semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: qring name = ideal expression ; Purpose: declares a quotient ring as the basering modulo ideal expression, and sets it as current basering. ideal expression has to be represented by a standard basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Singular computes in a quotient ring using the given representative of a polynomial and usually does not reduce w.r.t. the quotient ideal unless necessary; operations based on standard bases operate with residue classes; other operations act on polynomial objects; use fetch to map objects between rings and quotient rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novice ordering recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Remark: The novice user should generally use the ordering dp for computations in the polynomial ring K[x1, . . . , xn], resp. ds for computations in the localization Loc(x)K[x1, . . . , xn]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: dp and ds are good default choices; see Appendix B for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of term/orderings available
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular offers Global orderings (lp, rp, dp, Dp, lex, etc.), Local orderings (ls, rs, ds, Ds, ws, Ws), Matrix orderings M(intmat), Extra weight vector a(intvec) preceding an ordering, Product/block orderings (combination of above), and Module orderings (ordering,...,C or c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global orderings are well-orderings (1 < x); local orderings are not well-orderings; matrix orderings allow arbitrary compatible orderings but are slower; extra weight vectors and block combinations provide fine control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Module ordering semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Module orderings such as (ordering,...,C) sort polynomial vectors by monomial ordering first, then by components. (C ascending: gen(1) < gen(2) < ...; c descending).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Component ordering placement within a product ordering affects precedence: monomial blocks before component ordering have higher precedence, those after have lower precedence. Default is (ordering,...,C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and limitations for coefficient rings like Z and Z/n
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular supports coefficient rings which are not fields, i.e. the integers Z and the finite rings Z/n. These coefficient rings were implemented in Singular 3.0.5 and at the moment only limited functionality is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect restricted algorithm availability and possibly only approximate computations for certain numeric rings; p-adic computations approximated by Z/p^n with large n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard-basis is the basic algorithm; it supports many orderings
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic algorithm in Singular is a general standard basis algorithm for any monomial ordering which is compatible with the natural semi-group structure of the exponents. This includes well-orderings (Buchberger algorithm to compute a Groebner basis) and tangent cone orderings (Mora algorithm) as special cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many higher-level computations build on standard basis computations; choose ordering appropriately and prefer built-in heuristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command: facstd — factorizing Groebner basis algorithm
rubrics_metrics.description: facstd computes a list of Groebner bases via the Factorizing Groebner Basis Algorithm, i.e., their intersection has the same radical as the original ideal. It need not be a Groebner basis of the given ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use facstd when factorizing behavior and radical-intersection properties are desired rather than a single standard Groebner basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command: fglm requirements and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: fglm computes a Groebner basis provided that a reduced Groebner basis w.r.t. another ordering is given. Implements the FGLM algorithm. The given ideal must be zero-dimensional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use fglm to change ordering for zero-dimensional ideals when a reduced Groebner basis is available for a starting ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command: groebner preferred method
rubrics_metrics.description: groebner computes a standard resp. Groebner basis using a heuristically chosen method. This is the preferred method to compute a standard resp. Groebner basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer groebner for general-purpose standard/Groebner basis computations; heuristics choose a suitable method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commands for computing a Groebner in difficult orderings
rubrics_metrics.description: stdfglm computes a Groebner basis in a ring with a 'difficult' ordering (e.g., lexicographical) via std w.r.t. a 'simple' ordering and fglm. The given ideal must be zero-dimensional. stdhilb computes a Groebner basis in a difficult ordering guided by the Hilbert series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stdfglm or stdhilb when direct computation in lexicographical or other hard orderings is impractical; zero-dimensionality requirement applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions that require standard bases
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations based on standard bases (e.g. std, groebner, reduce) and functions which require a standard basis (e.g. dim, hilb, kbase) operate with residue classes; all others operate on polynomial objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure input ideals/modules are represented by standard bases when calling functions that require them; use reduce(f, std(0)) to explicitly reduce in a quotient ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commands for resolutions and their preconditions
rubrics_metrics.description: res computes a free resolution using a heuristically chosen method (preferred). fres (improved sres) computes a free resolution using Schreyer’s method — input must be a standard basis. lres requires homogeneous input. mres computes a minimal free resolution with the Syzygy method. sres requires standard basis; nres uses standard-basis method. syz computes the first syzygy module of given generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the resolution routine matching your input's properties (homogeneous, standard basis available) and desired output (minimal, Schreyer, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-processing resolution commands
rubrics_metrics.description: betti computes graded Betti numbers from a free resolution. minres minimizes a free resolution. regularity computes regularity from a minimal free resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute Betti numbers or regularity only after obtaining an appropriate (preferably minimal) free resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polynomial processing commands and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: char_series computes characteristic sets. extgcd computes extended gcd of two polynomials (univariate only). factorize computes factorization of univariate and multivariate polynomials (various algorithms described). gcd computes gcds (NTL or subresultant/EZGCD depending on case). resultant computes resultant of two univariate polynomials using subresultant algorithm (multivariate treated as univariate in a main variable). vandermonde interpolates a polynomial from values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of algorithmic differences depending on characteristic and whether polynomials are univariate/multivariate or over algebraic extensions; factorization reduces to univariate case and uses Hensel lifting for characteristic 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix and numeric algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: bareiss implements sparse Gauss-Bareiss for elimination in arbitrary integral domains. det computes determinant (modular algorithm for integer matrices, Gauss-Bareiss otherwise). minor computes all minors of given size. laguerre computes all complex roots of a univariate polynomial. uressolve finds all roots of a 0-dimensional ideal with multivariate resultants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use integer-optimized algorithms for integer matrices; numeric root-finders are available for univariate and 0-dimensional systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: option — control computation behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: option allows setting of options for manipulating the behavior of computations (such as reduction strategies) and for showing protocol information indicating the progress of a computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tune option settings to change reduction strategies, verbosity, and other computational parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: General language and command model
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular interprets commands given interactively on the command line as well as in user-defined procedures; there is no distinction in syntax/semantics between these cases. Major building blocks: expressions, commands, control structures (if, for, while).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand declarations, assignments, commands without return values, and print commands; use blocks { } for grouping and be aware of minor differences to C (see major differences section).

rubrics_metrics.name: General command syntax rules and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Declaration forms: type name = expression; alias type name; type name list = expression list; type name; Assignment: name = expression; name list = expression list (not simultaneous). Function without return value: function name[(argument list)]; Print command: expression ;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments are not expressions (no chained assignments). Use print or show for pretty output of complex types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special characters and operator semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: List of special characters and their meanings: = assignment, { } block parentheses, [ ] access operator, +, ++, -, --, *, /, %, ^, ==, !=, >=, <=, <, >, !, &&, ||, " string delimiter, ' name substitution, ? synonym for help, // and /* */ comments, ; statement separator, , and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note differences such as / vs div and that mod alias % yields non-negative result; ^ or ** exponentiation; use correct delimiters for strings and comments.
